title: Employees Earning Above Their Department Average
description:
Return every employee whose salary is **strictly above the average salary of their own department**.

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| salary | INT |
| department_id | INT |

Output columns: `name`, `salary`, `department_id`. Order by `department_id`, `salary` descending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, salary INT, department_id INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice',120000,1),(2,'Bob',80000,2),(3,'Carol',140000,1),(4,'Dan',70000,2),(5,'Eve',90000,2),(6,'Fay',100000,1);
solution_sql: SELECT name, salary, department_id FROM employees e WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees WHERE department_id = e.department_id) ORDER BY department_id, salary DESC

test_cases.description: Carol (140k) beats dept 1 avg 120k; Eve (90k) beats dept 2 avg 80k

hints: A correlated subquery references a column from the outer query (e.department_id).
It re-executes for every row in the outer query.
